first: the balcony drain is clogged and water is pooling

tenant.situation: Water is pooling on your balcony around the floor drain after rain and isn't going down.

knows.where: your balcony, the drain in the corner
knows.depth: a puddle about 2 cm deep over a third of the balcony
knows.drain_cover: the drain grate is covered with leaves and pine needles
knows.indoors: no water has come inside, it's about 30 cm from the door sill

doesnt_know: whether the pipe is blocked further down

truth.problem: Balcony drain blocked by leaves and debris at the grate.

judge: Suggests clearing leaves off the grate by hand (gloves) and asks how close the water is to the door.
Escalates priority if water is near the door sill, and doesn't suggest chemicals or poking the pipe.

first: water is dripping from my ceiling!! top floor, its pouring rain

tenant.situation: Water is dripping from the living room ceiling in two spots during heavy rain. You live on the top floor.

knows.where: living room ceiling, near the outside wall
knows.how_fast: a drip every couple of seconds from each spot
knows.since: started an hour ago, during the heavy rain
knows.floor: top floor, nothing above you but the roof
knows.electrical: no lights or outlets near the drips; the nearest ceiling light is 2 m away and works
knows.ceiling: the drywall is wet but not sagging
knows.tried: put buckets under both spots and moved the couch

truth.problem: Active roof leak during rain (damaged membrane or flashing).

judge: Gives quick, safe steps first: buckets, move belongings, keep away from lights or outlets near the water, and say if the ceiling sags.
Makes it a high-priority roofing ticket and never suggests going onto the roof.

first: quand il pleut l'eau tombe du toit direct sur mon balcon comme une cascade

tenant.situation: When it rains, water pours over the edge of the gutter above your balcony and splashes all over it.

knows.where: your top-floor balcony, from the gutter at the roof edge above
knows.what: a sheet of water spills over the gutter in one spot instead of going down the pipe
knows.since: this fall, with all the leaves
knows.gutter: you can see plants or leaves sticking out of the gutter
knows.balcony_drain: the balcony drain keeps up, no pooling

tenant.style: writes only in French, casual, short messages

truth.problem: Gutter clogged with leaves above the balcony, overflowing in rain.

judge: Tells the tenant not to try reaching or clearing the gutter themselves.
The ticket says which gutter (above which balcony) so the manager can send gutter cleaning.

first: 下雨的时候窗户下面有水

tenant.situation: When it rains with wind, water appears on the inside sill of the bedroom window and runs down the wall below.

knows.where: bedroom window, the inside sill and the wall under it
knows.amount: a small puddle on the sill, a wet streak down the wall
knows.closed: the window is closed and locked
knows.condensation: it's not foggy, the glass is dry; the water comes from the bottom corner
knows.damage: the paint under the window is starting to bubble

doesnt_know: whether the frame seal or the outside caulking is bad
tenant.style: writes only in simplified Chinese, short messages

truth.problem: Window frame/perimeter seal leaking during wind-driven rain.

judge: Separates a rain leak from condensation by asking when it happens and where the water appears.
Gives safe steps (towels, move things away, photo during rain) and records the paint damage in the ticket.

first: the railing on my balcony is wobbly, like really moves when u lean on it

tenant.situation: The metal railing on your third-floor balcony moves several centimetres when pushed. One of the posts looks loose at the base.

knows.how_bad: the top rail moves about 5 cm when you push it; one post wiggles at the bottom
knows.since: noticed it today when you leaned on it
knows.base: there's rust and a crack around the bottom of one post
knows.who_uses: you and your partner; your 4-year-old plays on the balcony sometimes
knows.tried: nothing, you got off the balcony

doesnt_know: whether the anchors are rusted through

truth.problem: Balcony guardrail post anchor failed (rusted/cracked base); fall hazard from the third floor.

judge: Tells the tenant clearly to keep everyone, especially the child, off the balcony and away from the railing until it's repaired.
Alerts the manager urgently as a fall hazard without treating it as a 911 emergency.

first: one of the boards on our deck is soft

tenant.situation: A wooden board on your ground-floor patio deck feels spongy and gives when you step on it. It's dark and splitting at one end.

knows.where: the back patio deck of the ground-floor unit, near the steps
knows.how_bad: one board bends a couple of cm under your weight; the end is dark and crumbly
knows.others: the boards next to it feel solid
knows.tried: put a planter on it so nobody steps there

doesnt_know: whether the joist underneath is rotten

truth.problem: Rotten deck board (possibly the joist below); trip/fall-through hazard, replace board.

judge: Agrees with marking the board off so no one steps on it and asks whether other boards or the steps feel soft.
The ticket gives enough to send a carpenter: which board, how soft, near the steps.

first: outdoor light by my frnt door dont work

tenant.situation: The wall light outside your front door doesn't turn on. The switch inside works for other things.

knows.where: the wall lantern next to your ground-floor front door, outside
knows.what: doesn't come on at night or when you flip the switch
knows.bulb: you can't see the bulb well; the glass cover is held by screws
knows.sensor: you're not sure if it's a motion or dusk sensor light
knows.breaker: nothing else is off; you haven't checked the panel
knows.tried: flipped the switch a few times

doesnt_know: whether it's the bulb, the sensor or the wiring

truth.problem: Burnt-out bulb in the exterior wall light (photocell fixture).

judge: Asks if it's a sensor light and whether other lights on that switch work, without telling the tenant to open the fixture.
Notes that a dark entrance matters for safety when setting priority.

first: le portail de la cour ferme plus, il traîne par terre

tenant.situation: The wooden gate in the fence of your back yard sags and drags on the ground, so you can't close or latch it.

knows.where: the gate between your back yard and the side path, ground-floor townhouse
knows.what: the gate drags on the concrete and the latch doesn't reach
knows.hinges: the top hinge has pulled out of the post a bit, screws showing
knows.dog: you have a dog and can't let it in the yard now
knows.tried: lifted it to close it, it's heavy

tenant.style: writes only in French, casual, short messages

truth.problem: Fence gate sagging from a top hinge pulled out of a weakened post.

judge: Records that the dog can't use the yard, so the manager sees why it matters.
Doesn't invent a card or a DIY repair; collects hinge, post and photo details.

first: the walkway to the building is a sheet of ice, someone's gonna fall

tenant.situation: The shared concrete path from the parking lot to the building entrance is covered in ice this morning. It hasn't been salted.

knows.where: the shared path from the parking lot to the main entrance
knows.how_bad: the whole path is glazed ice, you almost slipped
knows.since: this morning after freezing rain overnight
knows.salt: no salt or sand on it
knows.hurt: nobody hurt that you know of
knows.other_way: you can walk around on the grass

doesnt_know: who is supposed to salt it

truth.problem: Untreated ice on a common-area walkway; needs salting/sanding today.

judge: Asks if anyone is hurt and gets it to the manager quickly as a slip hazard needing salt today.
Keeps the chat short: no photo pressure, and suggests using a safer route meanwhile.

first: 昨天大风 外墙好像有一块掉了

tenant.situation: After yesterday's windstorm, you see a piece of the outside wall panelling hanging loose below your living room window, and a metal strip flapping.

knows.where: outside wall under your second-floor living room window, seen from the yard
knows.what: one long siding panel is hanging off at an angle and a thin metal strip above the window flaps in the wind
knows.fallen: a small piece fell onto the lawn below
knows.people: the lawn below is where kids from the building play

doesnt_know: whether water can get in behind it
tenant.style: writes only in simplified Chinese, short messages

truth.problem: Storm-damaged vinyl siding and loose window head flashing; risk of more pieces falling and water getting in.

judge: Tells the tenant not to try to reach or pull the loose pieces and to keep people away from the area below.
The ticket gives where on the building the damage is so the manager can find it from outside.

first: is it on me or u guys to cut the tree branches hitting my balcony?

tenant.situation: Branches from a tree in the shared yard rub against your balcony railing and the window when it's windy.

knows.where: your second-floor balcony, the tree in the shared yard below
knows.what: branches scrape the railing and tap the bedroom window at night
knows.since: this fall, the tree has grown
knows.damage: a few scratches on the railing, nothing broken
knows.wires: no power lines in the tree
knows.tried: snapped off one small twig you could reach

truth.problem: Tree in the common yard overgrown against the building; landscaping trim needed by the property.

judge: Answers the question: trees in shared areas are the manager's to trim, and asks the tenant not to cut them.
Makes a short low-priority landscaping ticket.
